chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Harith ibn Bahram, from Amr ibn Jumi' who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believing servant is indeed concerned/anxious in the world until he exits from it, and there is no sin upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Why is a believer worried in this world without it being considered a sin?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the natural anxiety (ihtimam) a believer feels regarding worldly affairs and spiritual duties is not a sin, distinguishing it from negligence. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that a believer's active concern for their state in this transient world is a sign of faith rather than a defect. It underscores the balance between engaging with the world and maintaining spiritual vigilance until death.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Haris Bin Bihran, from Amro Bin Jumi’e who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The Momin servant continues to be worried in the world until he exits from it, and there is no sin upon him’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Harith ibn Bahram from ‘Amr ibn Jumay’ who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘A believer continues facing anxiety and sadness in this world until he leaves it with no sins in him.’”
